title: Percentage axis fits the data when no value is above 200%
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in one location (workplace) with technician clocked time over the last twelve months.
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. The workplace has technician time this year where every technician's monthly Technician Utilization is 100% or less (utilization can never pass 100%, so this always holds).
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Set the Technician Utilization pill to Last 12 Months.
  3. Click View details on the Technician Utilization tile.
  4. Hover the highest point and read its value.
  5. Read the top label of the left-hand axis.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The highest point reads 100% or less.
  • The axis fits the data: its top label is the first gridline at or just above the highest value (e.g. 100%), not 200%.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9581 (Story 9, Chart Behavior); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 9. Split out of C88621. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) board 07_TechUtil_After (axis 0% to 100%), used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R1: “A percentage chart's value axis fits the range of the data shown.”
  • S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
